pipeline_name: West Esh El-Mallaha-Gebel Az Zeit Oil Pipeline

validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/SPEC: confirmed real. Oil & Gas Journal, 'Lukoil commissions export pipeline in Egypt' (contemporaneous, Oct 2004) independently describes 'a 100 km oil pipeline connecting Khurghada, Egypt, to General Petroleum Co.'s Ras El Bikhar terminal and the Geisum terminal at Gebel Az Zeit', 'designed to transport as much as 24,000 b/d of oil from the West Esh El-Mallaha (WEEM) block', 'The $8 million pipeline', commissioned by Lukoil Overseas Holding Ltd (holds 50% of the WEEM concession) in October 2004. Every core GEM value matches this single primary trade-press source exactly: Fuel=Oil, LengthKnown=100 km, Capacity=24,000 bpd, Cost=$8,000,000 (article states '$8 million', a prose/unit equivalence -- the existing Cost [ref] on this same OGJ URL was flagged by the automated checker as 'value not found' only because it looked for the digit string '8,000,000' and missed the prose form; the ref IS valid and should NOT be treated as unsupported), StartYear1=2004, Operator=Lukoil Overseas Holding Ltd, FuelSource=West Esh El-Mallaha, EndLocation=Ras El Bikhar terminal, EndPrefecture/District=Gebel Az Zeit. Classification (crude oil field-to-terminal export line) is correct -- this is not a products/LPG line and does not belong in GGIT. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against the full 46-row Egypt-oil roster -- no other row shares this name, these endpoints, or this field (WEEM/West Esh El-Mallaha is unique to this row); not a relabel or segment double-count of any other PID. CAVEAT (why not 'high'): only ONE independent source could be verified this session. The gem.wiki page's second citation, Rigzone 'Lukoil Hits 2 Million Ton Mark at WEEM Field...', is BLOCKED, not deleted -- it returns HTTP 403 directly and via url_verifier (TooManyRedirects/anti-bot behavior on this old article URL), and has zero Wayback Machine snapshots (CDX query empty, /wayback/available returns an empty archived_snapshots object) -- so it could not be read or cited, and per standing rules this is not treated as evidence against the pipeline. WebSearch quota was exhausted this session (200/200) before a second independent source could be located, so tier is capped at medium pending a future search for corroboration (e.g. Lukoil Overseas annual reports, EGPC yearbooks, or a re-fetch of the Rigzone URL). SECONDARY CAVEAT (attribution, low severity): GEM's StartLocation value is 'Easern desert' (also misspelled) -- a vague regional descriptor. The OGJ source is explicit that the pipeline's origin point is 'Khurghada' (Hurghada), which is consistent with StartPrefecture/District='Hurgada' already on the row but more specific than the StartLocation value itself. Recommend correcting StartLocation to 'Hurghada' (or 'Khurghada') to match the sourced route description and fixing the 'Easern'->'Eastern' typo; not staging a ref for the current StartLocation value since the source does not literally support 'Eastern desert' as the specific origin name. This is a precision/spelling fix, not an existence or duplicate concern.

fills.researcher_notes: Article is entirely about this crude oil pipeline ('a 100 km oil pipeline... of oil from the West Esh El-Mallaha (WEEM) block').

Confirms commissioning/start of operations Oct 2004. No independent evidence located of any subsequent shutdown or cancellation -- continued 'operating' status is the reasonable read for an active field-export line with no contrary signal, consistent with GEM's own 2023 update.
Article headline event is the October 2004 commissioning; StartMonth1 was blank and is deep-filled as 'October' alongside the already-present StartYear1=2004.
'designed to transport as much as 24,000 b/d of oil' -- exact match.
'the West Esh El-Mallaha (WEEM) block' -- exact match, confirms this is the source field feeding the pipeline.

'General Petroleum Co.'s Ras El Bikhar terminal and the Geisum terminal at Gebel Az Zeit' -- exact match on both EndLocation and EndPrefecture/District. Article also names a second terminus, the Geisum terminal, not separately recorded on the row -- not staged as a change, just noted.
Article: 'Lukoil Overseas Holding Ltd. has commissioned...' and 'Lukoil Overseas holds 50% of the concession' -- exact match on Operator.

summary: P5122 confirmed (caveat): real, correctly classified WEEM-field export line; every value (length 100 km, capacity 24,000 bpd, cost $8M, start Oct 2004, operator, fuel source, end terminal) matches Oil & Gas Journal's 2004 commissioning article exactly (8 REFS_ADDED, existing Cost ref reaffirmed as valid despite an automated false-negative), and no duplicate found against the 46-row roster. Tier capped at medium -- only one independent source verifiable this session; the wiki's second citation (Rigzone) is a live 403/redirect-loop block with zero Wayback coverage (UNRESOLVED, not evidence against the pipeline), and WebSearch quota was exhausted before a substitute could be found. One low-severity attribution flag: StartLocation='Easern desert' is a vague/misspelled regional descriptor where the source names 'Khurghada' specifically -- recommend correcting to 'Hurghada'.
